Tow Côja Tiny Home Is a Rustic Retreat With Three Double Beds and a Charming Rooftop Deck
12 photos
Photo: Madeiguincho
Some people choose to live tiny to gain financial freedom, others are into it for the sustainability factor, and others are simply looking for personal liberation. But regardless of the reason behind their decision, tiny home living isn’t just a trend anymore. It has become a lifestyle, a deliberate choice towards simplicity and sustainable living.
Even though, lately, tiny houses have been getting bigger and more luxurious in some parts of the world, there are still builders who craft simple, practical tiny homes that allow dwellers to embrace a minimalist, less consumption-oriented lifestyle. One of them is Madeiguincho, a Portugal-based woodworking and architecture atelier that focused on craftsmanship, sustainable timber construction, and spatial efficiency.
The studio has been around since 1990 and builds absolutely stunning wooden tiny houses that feel right at home in any natural environment. This builder’s models are not just a place to live or a shelter, but a place of comfort where you can live more in harmony with the surrounding nature.
This talented team’s latest creation is Tow Côja, a tiny house on wheels designed as a minimalist, peaceful retreat that exudes rustic cabin vibes and proves that, when thoughtfully used, space is more than just a number. Though it has a footprint of only 17 square meters (183 square feet), this compact dwelling holds more than you might expect.
Photo: Madeiguincho It boasts a dual-loft layout and can perfectly serve as a retreat for family vacations, as it can accommodate up to six people in its three double beds. It also includes an open living room, a kitchen, and a bathroom. But with two glass double doors, large windows, and a rooftop deck, this is a tiny home that not only keeps you connected to your surroundings but also encourages you to spend time outside.
Built on a dual-axle trailer, this compact dwelling can be towed to your preferred spot in nature and also offers the possibility of relocation. Its exterior is clad in dark burnt wood, giving the home a traditional, rustic appearance, and multiple windows with natural wood frames break up the dark facade on both levels, adding a warmer touch and allowing ample daylight to filter inside.
But the most distinctive feature when viewed from the outside is the split roof design. Two elevated roof sections add architectural interest and flank a recessed central area that has been configured as a wooden rooftop deck. Accessible from the upper level of the tiny home, this terrace provides a nice spot to relax and enjoy panoramic views of the surroundings.
Photo: Madeiguincho One of the glass entry doors leads into the central kitchen area, while the second one opens the living room to the outside. Both keep the interior open, bright, and airy, allowing for seamless indoor-outdoor living, something that many tiny home dwellers are looking for.
Tow Côja’s interior exudes a cabin feel, with an exquisite rustic aesthetic that combines several types of natural wood, including birch plywood panels, cedar, pine wood, and more. Environmentally friendly, durable, and high-quality, the different types of timber that adorn the interior walls, ceiling, and floors help create a warm and cozy ambiance.
The layout is open-plan and highly functional, maximizing the limited square footage. The kitchen occupies the center of the house, flanked by the living room on the left and the bathroom on the right. Simple wood ladders provide access to the two lofts, each positioned at either end of the house.
Photo: Madeiguincho The living room is bathed in natural light and is kept simple and minimalist , with just a built-in sofa bench with integrated storage and custom cushions. But that’s the setup during the day, because at night, the space transforms into a sleeping space thanks to a Murphy bed that’s neatly integrated next to the sofa. It stays flush against the wall when not needed, leaving ample room to move around, but it’s there when you want an extra bed.
A classic black cast-iron wood-burning stove is included between the living area and the kitchen. Placed on a protective floor plate, it adds another rustic touch, contributing to the cozy, warm atmosphere.
Minimalist in design but complete in terms of functionality, the kitchen is aligned against one wall and stands out with its country aesthetic featuring plywood cabinets and hardwood countertops. It offers enough storage space for cooking utensils and supplies and comes equipped with a black inset sink, an induction cooktop, and a full-size fridge that is hidden from view. Hooks, open shelves, and a long ledge make it easy to keep essentials within easy reach, and owners can also add plug-in appliances to add even more functionality to the space.
Photo: Madeiguincho Just like the rest of the house, the bathroom blends modern minimalism with warm, natural wood elements. It features a large shower, a matte black toilet, and a matching black vessel sink mounted on a simple wooden washstand. Above it hangs a round, black-framed mirror. The space is wrapped in contrasting wood finishes, combining light plywood panels on one side with rich vertical timber boards on the other, and a dark charcoal ceiling overhead. And the nicest perk is that it benefits from its own entry door, for direct access from the outside.
With low ceilings and not much space for anything else besides the queen mattresses, the lofts inside the Tow Côja are clearly designed just for sleeping.
There is no mention of whether this particular unit is designed for off-grid living, but typically, Madeiguincho offers a series of self-sufficiency features, such as solar panels, a battery system, rain-collection systems, dry composting toilets, and more.
Cozy, beautifully styled, and highly functional, the Tow Côja tiny home proves that small-space living is not about what you give up when downsizing but rather about concentrating on what really matters.
